title: Slurry Pump

introduction.definition: A slurry pump is a heavy-duty centrifugal pump built to move liquids carrying abrasive solids. It uses thick, replaceable wear parts — hard-metal (high-chrome white iron) or rubber liners, a large slow-running impeller with thick vanes and expelling vanes — and is designed so that the parts that wear can be changed quickly. Wear, not efficiency, usually governs its selection and operating speed.
applications: Alumina refineries: bauxite slurry, red mud, digestion and precipitation circuits
Mineral processing: mill discharge, cyclone feed, tailings
Power plants: ash and FGD (limestone/gypsum) slurry
key_points: Wear ∝ (velocity)^~2.5–3 — run as slowly as possible
Expeller + gland seal or mechanical seal
Head and efficiency derating for solids (ANSI/HI 12.1-12.6)

classification.configuration: Horizontal, end suction, lined, overhung, belt-driven

introduction.summary: A heavy centrifugal pump built to move abrasive mixtures of liquid and solids (mine tailings, dredge spoil, mineral concentrates). Large, slow-running impellers with thick shrouds and wide passages limit wear; the wetted surfaces are replaceable liners of hard white iron or rubber held in a split outer casing. Pump-out vanes on the impeller and an expeller behind it keep slurry away from the gland. Speed is set by the V-belt ratio, so the duty can be matched without trimming the impeller.

what_to_look_for: Slurry enters the suction through the throatbush, which is the most heavily worn liner part.
The large, thick-vaned impeller accelerates the slurry; vane inlet edges and the front shroud wear fastest.
Pump-out vanes on the impeller shrouds reduce recirculation through the clearances and protect the seal area.

steps.text: Slurry enters the suction through the throatbush, which is the most heavily worn liner part.
The large, thick-vaned impeller accelerates the slurry; vane inlet edges and the front shroud wear fastest.
Pump-out vanes on the impeller shrouds reduce recirculation through the clearances and protect the seal area.
The volute liner collects the flow; the cutwater (tongue) suffers severe erosion.
The expeller keeps slurry away from the gland while running; gland packing seals at standstill.
A heavy bearing cartridge on an adjustable pedestal lets the impeller be moved forward to keep the front clearance closed as parts wear.
V-belts let the speed be matched exactly to the duty so the pump runs no faster than necessary.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Flatter curve than a water pump; head and efficiency fall with solids concentration and particle size (derating factors HR, ER).

wear.title: Wear zones
wear.description: Typical wear pattern of a centrifugal slurry pump. Purple = most severe: throatbush face and impeller front shroud gap (recirculation gouging), impeller eye / vane inlet edges, and the volute cutwater (tongue). Pink = moderate: volute liner around the impeller tip and vane trailing edges. Yellow = light: frame-plate liner / back shroud. Wear grows steeply with particle size, solids concentration and velocity, so slurry pumps run slow and keep the front clearance closed.

parts.name: Outer Casing (Cover & Frame Plates)
parts.function: Pressure-containing outer casing that supports the liners.

parts.name: Volute Liner & Throatbush (Hard Metal)
parts.function: Replaceable wear-resistant hydraulic passage (volute) and suction throatbush.
parts.material: High-chrome white iron (~27% Cr), natural rubber, polyurethane, ceramics.

parts.name: Closed Impeller with Pump-Out Vanes
parts.function: Adds energy to the slurry; pump-out vanes reduce recirculation and pressure at the shaft seal.
parts.material: High-chrome white iron, rubber-covered steel, polyurethane.

parts.name: Frame-Plate Liner Insert & Stuffing Box
parts.function: Back liner of the pump chamber and housing for the expeller and gland.

parts.name: Expeller (Dynamic Seal)
parts.function: Centrifugal (dynamic) seal: its vanes generate pressure that stops slurry reaching the gland while running.

parts.name: Gland Packing, Lantern Ring & Gland Follower
parts.function: Seals the shaft at standstill (with expeller) or continuously (with gland water flush).
parts.material: PTFE/aramid/graphite braided packing; bronze lantern ring.

parts.name: Bearing Cartridge Housing
parts.function: Holds the shaft bearings and oil or grease, and supports the overhung impeller.

parts.name: Roller Bearings (Wet End & Drive End)
parts.function: Carries radial load near the impeller end.

parts.name: Pedestal Base (with Bearing Adjustment)
parts.function: Provides a rigid common mounting for pump and driver, maintains alignment and transfers loads to the foundation.
parts.material: Carbon steel, painted; stainless steel for hygienic or corrosive areas.

parts.name: Shaft & Shaft Sleeve
parts.function: Transmits torque from the coupling to the impeller(s).
parts.material: Carbon steel, 4140 alloy steel, 410/420 or 316 stainless, duplex.

parts.name: Pump Sheave (V-Belt Pulley)
parts.function: Driven pulley; sheave ratio sets pump speed.

parts.name: Motor Sheave
parts.function: Driving pulley on the motor.

parts.name: V-Belts
parts.function: Transmit power from motor to pump sheave.

parts.name: Belt Guard
parts.function: Prevents contact with rotating parts.
parts.material: Steel, aluminium or non-sparking brass for hazardous areas.

parts.name: Overhead Motor Mount
parts.function: Supports the motor above the pump and allows belt tensioning.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Frame & End Shields

foundation: Heavy foundation; slurry pumps see high vibration from solids.
alignment: Belt drives: sheave alignment and belt tension per manufacturer.
piping: Short, straight suction with large-radius bends; avoid high points where solids settle or air collects.
commissioning: Start on water, then introduce slurry.
Set gland water pressure/flow where a flushed gland is used.

routine.task: Check gland leakage and gland water.

periodic.task: Adjust impeller front clearance by moving the bearing cartridge forward.

overhaul.task: Replace throatbush, impeller and volute liner as a set when worn.
Measure wear thickness to predict the next change-out.

lubrication: Grease-lubricated roller bearings (some oil); purge with care — slurry contamination kills bearings.

remedies: Lower speed; harder material; adjust clearance

symptoms: Deep grooves on throatbush face and front shroud
Pressure rise then loss of flow

causes: Slurry ingress into the bearing housing

script.narration: This module introduces the Slurry Pump.
A slurry pump is a heavy-duty centrifugal pump built to move liquids carrying abrasive solids.

It uses thick, replaceable wear parts — hard-metal (high-chrome white iron) or rubber liners, a large slow-running impeller with thick vanes and expelling vanes — and is designed so that the parts that wear can be changed quickly.
Wear, not efficiency, usually governs its selection and operating speed.

Typical applications include alumina refineries: bauxite slurry, red mud, digestion and precipitation circuits; mineral processing: mill discharge, cyclone feed, tailings; dredging and sand/gravel; power plants: ash and FGD (limestone/gypsum) slurry.

video_tutorials.title: Slurry Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Slurry Pump.
Check gland leakage and gland water.
Check vibration and bearing temperature.
Adjust impeller front clearance by moving the bearing cartridge forward.
Retension V-belts.
Replace throatbush, impeller and volute liner as a set when worn.
Measure wear thickness to predict the next change-out.
Watch for abrasive wear: falling head and flow. Common cause: high velocity.
Watch for recirculation gouging at the throatbush: deep grooves on throatbush face and front shroud. Common cause: open front clearance.
Watch for pipeline blockage: pressure rise then loss of flow. Common cause: velocity below settling velocity.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
